messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
int sum(int a[], int n) { return a[n - 1] + sum(a, n - 1); }
// a = {1, 2, 3}

Question: What is sum(a, 3)?
The student answered: 6

The student holds this wrong belief and does not know it is wrong: Recursion stops by itself when the work is done

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: sure of themselves, plain English, one sentence of 8 to 18 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["The function adds 3 then 2 then 1 and stops when there is nothing left to add.", "Since a[n-1] gives the last element, it works backward until the total is done on its own.", "Each call adds the next number and the adding just finishes naturally at the end.", "The recursion keeps going down until all three numbers are used up and the sum is complete.", "It just keeps calling itself and the calls end when the whole sum of 1, 2, 3 is reached."]}

sentences: The function adds 3 then 2 then 1 and stops when there is nothing left to add.
Since a[n-1] gives the last element, it works backward until the total is done on its own.
Each call adds the next number and the adding just finishes naturally at the end.
The recursion keeps going down until all three numbers are used up and the sum is complete.
It just keeps calling itself and the calls end when the whole sum of 1, 2, 3 is reached.
